title: Allied Health Clinician: Review a Community Handoff Gap
prompt: You are an allied health clinician reviewing fictional Rowan Team's community handoff. Supplied artifact: "Person agrees to referral. Community team will visit Friday. Transport arranged. Close coordination task." Supporting records show only an emailed referral, a transport quote without booking confirmation, and the person's note: "Please call me before anyone comes to my home." Exercise policy requires receiving-team acceptance, agreed contact preferences, and confirmation of any stated bookings; clinical readiness decisions belong to the responsible clinical team. Review the artifact and write a corrected coordination note. Do not select treatment or determine whether a transition is clinically safe.
blurb: Expose assumed visits and bookings, preserve the person's preferences, and assign the missing confirmations.

rubric.label: Audit the handoff claims
rubric.description: Compares each claim with its actual supporting record.

anchors.0: Repeats Friday visit and transport as confirmed.
anchors.2: Flags that referral acceptance and transport booking are unconfirmed.
anchors.4: Separates email sent, acceptance unknown, quoted transport, and the person's prior-call preference; removes the unsupported closure and Friday promise.

rubric.label: Honor the contact preference
rubric.description: Turns consent and access preferences into usable next steps.

anchors.0: Treats referral consent as permission for any unannounced visit.
anchors.2: Records the request for a call before a home visit.
anchors.4: Confirms preferred contact with the person, passes only necessary information with the agreed referral, and asks the receiving team to acknowledge the pre-visit call requirement.

rubric.label: Assign confirmation and update owners
rubric.description: Closes coordination gaps without claiming clinical authority.

anchors.0: Closes because emails have been sent or personally declares readiness.
anchors.2: Assigns follow-up for referral and transport and leaves coordination open.
anchors.4: Names a responsible coordinator for each confirmation, sets an agreed update, escalates unresolved transition questions to the clinical team, and states exactly which evidence permits each coordination item to close.

reference.scenario: You are an allied health clinician reviewing fictional Rowan Team's community handoff. Supplied artifact: "Person agrees to referral. Community team will visit Friday. Transport arranged. Close coordination task." Supporting records show only an emailed referral, a transport quote without booking confirmation, and the person's note: "Please call me before anyone comes to my home." Exercise policy requires receiving-team acceptance, agreed contact preferences, and confirmation of any stated bookings; clinical readiness decisions belong to the responsible clinical team. Review the artifact and write a corrected coordination note. Do not select treatment or determine whether a transition is clinically safe.

facts.value: The community intake desk is open today. Friday was an internal target, not a date offered by the receiving team.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks where Friday came from

facts.value: The person can receive a phone call this afternoon and has not agreed to a home-visit time. A coordinator can verify transport availability after an actual appointment is agreed.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about preferences or coordination sequence

model_points: There are three unsupported assumptions: accepted referral, agreed visit, and booked transport. A complete coordination note preserves the actual evidence and pending states.
Referral consent does not erase an explicit preference to be called. Arrange agreement on a visit before presenting it as scheduled or booking linked transport.
Keep clinical readiness decisions with the clinical team. For coordination, seek accountable confirmations and update the person even if a service has not replied.

probes.trigger: candidate changes wording to pending but gives no follow-up owner
probes.question: Who will obtain each confirmation and tell the person the outcome?

probes.trigger: candidate chooses a joint call with the person and receiving team
probes.question: Which permissions and unresolved arrangements would the call need to address?

probes.trigger: candidate first repeats Friday as booked then corrects
probes.question: How would you repair the expectation without promising a replacement date?

fair_alternatives: A joint call or separate contacts can both work when consent, preferences, and ownership are clear.
An evidence table or revised narrative may be used; do not require a particular health-record template.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess continuity and coordination across rehabilitation services. Do not infer diagnosis, prescribe therapy, or judge discharge safety. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess continuity and coordination across rehabilitation services. Do not infer diagnosis, prescribe therapy, or judge discharge safety. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Separate coordination from clinical decisions
learning_drills.prompt: Create a three-row handoff table for referral, visit agreement, and transport with evidence, unknown, and next owner. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Do not equate referral with acceptance
Link transport to an agreed appointment
Keep clinical readiness outside the coordination claim
